summary.title: Distributed Systems Classics
summary.one_liner: A curated reading list of ten influential distributed systems papers, from Lamport's logical clocks to Raft, as a starting point for the field.
keywords: where to start reading distributed systems
takeaways: The list covers foundational results on logical time, global snapshots, and fault-tolerant consensus.
It includes the FLP impossibility result and the Byzantine Generals problem.
Consensus protocols listed are Viewstamped Replication, Paxos (The Part-Time Parliament and Paxos Made Simple), and Raft.
Also included are Bitcoin's peer-to-peer cash paper and the CRDT paper on replicated data types.
The page is intended as an entry point to understand the problem space, with each entry linking to the original paper.
summary.summary: The page is a curated list of ten papers in distributed systems, presented as a starting point for understanding the field. Each entry gives the authors, year, title, and a link to the paper (DOI or publisher page). The papers span logical clocks (Lamport 1978), Byzantine fault tolerance, distributed snapshots, the FLP impossibility result, and several consensus protocols including Viewstamped Replication, Paxos, and Raft. It also includes Bitcoin's whitepaper and the CRDT paper. The page gives no commentary on the papers beyond the list itself.
